channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Neocloud Groq Aims to Double Value to $8 Billion Amid AI Selloff
item.description: A top executive at data center operator Groq has kicked off an audacious bid to double its valuation in about three months while slamming rivals in the space for being too reliant on debt markets.
item.dc:creator: Sridhar Natarajan and Natasha Mascarenhas

item.title: AI Selloff Exposes Data Center Boom Risks
item.description: The selloff in AI stocks is adding new uncertainty to the massive buildout of data centers across the US. Jolienne Halisky, CFO of AIB Data Centers, says financing for new projects could become more expensive and take longer as lenders reassess risk, while permitting, power and chip availability remain constraints. She joins Bloomberg Businessweek Daily to discuss her company's plans for its first Texas data center, concerns surrounding its anchor tenant Nebius, and why she believes the recent AI market rout will prove temporary. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Big Take: The New AI Trade Is FOGO
item.description: Wall Street’s AI rout sent US and then Asian markets tumbling, raising fresh questions about the sustainability of the global AI boom and where the next opportunities lie. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: OpenAI Completes $11 Billion Portion of Funding at $1.25 Trillion Value
item.description: OpenAI has closed on new funding of roughly $11 billion, the initial part of a round that values the company at $1.25 trillion, according to people familiar with the matter.The funding was wired to the company as of Friday, said the people, who spoke on condition of anonymity as the information is not public. The remainder of the round, which could increase to as much as $20 billion in total, is expected to be completed in the coming weeks, one person said.The AI developer has been in talks for
item.dc:creator: Natasha Mascarenhas and Rebecca Torrence

item.title: Brookfield CEO Says Infrastructure Is Growing Fastest
item.description: Brookfield Asset Management raised $25 billion in the third quarter, driven by credit and infrastructure, as the money manager positions itself as a key player funding the build-out of artificial intelligence. He speaks to Bloomberg's Dani Burger. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Time to Move Forward With 'Sensible' AI Regulation, Says Rep. Liccardo
item.description: Democrat Representative from California Sam Liccardo said that congress has 'issued a lot of press releases' on issues surrounding technology, but haven't managed to push meaningful legislation over the finish line. Liccardo, whose district includes parts of Silicon Valley, said it is critical lawmakers act on AI concerns and that it is time to move forward with 'sensible' regulation. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Power On: How Private Is an Always-Listening Apple Watch?
item.description:
Apple is bringing some its most ambitious AI capabilities to its products. As AI becomes increasingly woven into daily life, questions over privacy are likely to follow.
On this episode of the Power On podcast, Mark Gurman and Vlad Savov discuss privacy implications of new always-listening Apple Watch features. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Data Center Delays Risk an ‘Air Gap’ for Chips: Lovell
item.description: Nadia Lovell, head of global equity strategy at UBS Global Wealth Management, says data center delays could create an “air gap” for semiconductors, pressuring inventories, prices and margins. She favors compute over memory and hyperscalers with existing capacity. She speaks on “Bloomberg Surveillance.” (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Google Takes Over Wyoming Data Center That Crusoe Had Pitched
item.description: Alphabet Inc.’s Google has bought out Crusoe’s data center site in southeast Wyoming, opting to take on the project itself after the AI computing upstart failed to lock in customers.
item.dc:creator: Lynn Doan

item.title: Onsemi Scraps Plan for $2 Billion Expansion in Czech Republic
item.description: ON Semiconductor Corp. scrapped plans for a semiconductor expansion in the Czech Republic that was initially valued at as much as $2 billion.
item.dc:creator: Michal Kubala

item.title: OpenAI Staffer Pleads Not Guilty to Office Bugging Charge
item.description: An OpenAI engineer charged with planting a hidden recording device in one of the company’s offices pleaded not guilty in federal court.
item.dc:creator: Rachel Metz

item.title: Tech Stocks Rebound as Dip Buyers Return to AI Trade
item.description: Bloomberg’s Tim Stenovec takes a look at what's driving a rebound in tech stocks as dip buyers step in to support the battered AI trade. Plus, Anthropic's IPO plans are hit by the post-election selloff, prompting prospective investors to rethink the company's expected valuation; and the CEOs of Lyft and DraftKings join to break down their earnings results. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: How Fast-Money Systematic Funds Stoked $2.3T Tech Rout
item.description: As investors rushed out of US technology stocks on Thursday, selling by trend-following systematic strategies amplified what quickly became a record plunge by market value in the Nasdaq 100 index. Bloomberg's Natalia Kniazhevich joins Tim Stenovec on “Bloomberg Tech.” (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Anthropic IPO Investors Weigh Valuation as Low as $1.2 Trillion
item.description: Anthropic's IPO plans are running into a punishing post-election selloff, prompting a rethink among prospective investors of the company's expected valuation, which could now be as low as $1.2 trillion, according to sources. Bloomberg's Seth Fiegerman joins Tim Stenovec on “Bloomberg Tech.” (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Jobs Boom Meets AI Market Turmoil
item.description: Get a jump start on the US trading day with Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Open Interest." A blowout jobs report fuels expectations for another Fed rate hike, even as Wall Street reels from a nearly $4 trillion tech selloff and mounting questions about the AI trade. Plus, Anthropic's IPO prospects and valuation reset, BlackRock CIO Rick Rieder explains the AI unwind and emerging credit opportunities, Kevin Hassett, director of the White House National Economic Council, discusses inflation and Fed policy, and Greg Ebel, CEO of Enbridge Energy, weighs in on the growing energy demands of AI infrastructure. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Microsoft Winding Down Oracle Deal to Rent AI Cloud Capacity
item.description: Microsoft Corp. is winding down an arrangement to rent AI computing from Oracle Corp., part of a larger reassessment of billions of dollars in cloud partnerships.
item.dc:creator: Brody Ford

item.title: SpaceX Embrace of Compute Deals Eases Reliance on US Contracts
item.description: SpaceX’s reliance on US government-funded contracts will continue to shrink, Elon Musk said, signaling a shift in focus away from what was previously his rocket-launch company’s most important partnership.
item.dc:creator: Loren Grush and Carmen Arroyo

item.title: S&P 500 Posts Biggest Weekly Drop Since 2025 on AI Trade Worries
item.description: US stocks logged their biggest weekly loss since April 2025 on concerns over the artificial intelligence trade after Democrats swept the US midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Natalia Kniazhevich

item.title: Bitcoin Steadies After Record Hack Fallout, Midterm Turbulence
item.description: Bitcoin settled near recent lows after a bruising selloff on Thursday swept through cryptocurrencies and other risky assets, pressured by lackluster chipmaker earnings and a Democratic sweep of Congress.
item.dc:creator: Emily Nicolle

item.title: Lone Pine, Whale Rock, Tiger Global Battered by AI Jitters
item.description: Lone Pine Capital, Tiger Global Management and Whale Rock Capital Management were among stock-picking hedge funds that were pummeled last month as concerns over AI investments roiled markets.
item.dc:creator: Hema Parmar
